name: What Is the Best Way to Plan Kitchen Lighting During a Remodel?

mainEntity.name: How many types of lighting should a remodeled San Diego kitchen have, and where should each one go?
mainEntity.text: How many types of lighting should a remodeled San Diego kitchen have, and where should each one go?

acceptedAnswer.text: Kitchen lighting works best in layers. Ambient fixtures provide general illumination, task lights brighten counters and sinks, and decorative or accent fixtures support the island, dining area, or glass-front cabinets. The correct number and location depend on ceiling height, room dimensions, cabinet depth, finish reflectivity, and the user’s vision needs. Plan lighting with the cabinet elevations and appliance layout. Under-cabinet fixtures should be positioned toward the front of the cabinet so the work surface is illuminated instead of the wall. Recessed lights should avoid being hidden behind tall cabinets, and pendants should not interfere with sightlines or hood placement. Include dimmers and separate controls for cooking, prep, dining, and nighttime use. Choose color temperature and color-rendering performance appropriate for food preparation and finishes. Confirm fixture dimensions, driver access, ventilation conflicts, and electrical box locations before rough-in. Ask for a reflected ceiling plan and switching diagram rather than relying on a decorative rendering. Lighting changes become expensive after drywall, backsplash, or cabinets are installed.
acceptedAnswer.description: A functional kitchen usually combines ambient lighting, task lighting, and accent or decorative lighting. Place task lights so cabinets do not cast shadows on work surfaces, coordinate recessed fixtures with cabinet and island layouts, and provide switching that separates cooking, dining, and display areas. Finalize lighting before electrical rough-in and cabinet fabrication.
